sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: On the campus of Florida International University in Miami, there's a place ominously named the Extreme Events Institute.
sentences.zh: 在迈阿密的佛罗里达国际大学校园里，有一个名字听起来很不祥的地方，叫“极端事件研究所”。

sentences.en: They do things like map the risk of storm surge for the whole Caribbean and study how the public perceives the threat from natural disasters.
sentences.zh: 他们做的事情包括绘制整个加勒比地区的风暴潮风险地图，以及研究公众如何看待自然灾害的威胁。

sentences.en: They're also home to the International Hurricane Research Center.
sentences.zh: 他们也是国际飓风研究中心的所在地。

sentences.en: And right there, next to a parking lot in front of an open field, they have this huge, bright blue airplane hangar.
sentences.zh: 就在那里，停车场旁边，一片开阔地的前面，有一个巨大的、亮蓝色的飞机机库。

sentences.en: That's producer Alana Casanova-Burgess.
sentences.zh: 那是制片人阿拉娜·卡萨诺瓦-伯吉斯。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Here I am.
sentences.zh: 我到了。

sentences.en: Written across the massive closed doors in big baby blue letters, it says W-O-W.
sentences.zh: 在巨大的封闭门上，用淡蓝色的大字母写着“W-O-W”。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Which stands for Wall of Wind.
sentences.zh: 代表“风之墙”。

sentences.en: Aha!
sentences.zh: 啊哈！

sentences.en: Hi!
sentences.zh: 嗨！

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: They let you in, huh?
sentences.zh: 他们让你进来了，是吧？

sentences.en: Eric Salna, a meteorologist who works here, takes me inside the closed hangar.
sentences.zh: 在这里工作的气象学家埃里克·萨尔纳带我走进了封闭的机库。

sentences.en: He notices the recorder I'm holding and the mic I have shoved in his face.
sentences.zh: 他注意到了我手里拿着的录音机，还有我怼到他脸上的麦克风。

sentences.en: Your hands are full.
sentences.zh: 你手头挺忙的啊。

sentences.en: I was going to let you have the unique experience of opening one of the doors.
sentences.zh: 我本来想让你体验一下亲手打开其中一扇门的独特感受。

sentences.en: I could, I could.
sentences.zh: 我可以，我可以。

sentences.en: Look, look.
sentences.zh: 看，看。

sentences.en: He passes me a metal box with a big button.
sentences.zh: 他递给我一个带大按钮的金属盒。

sentences.en: So you're going to press that open.
sentences.zh: 所以，你要按下那个按钮打开它。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: And I kind of get the sense he does this with a lot of visitors.
sentences.zh: 我感觉他经常这样对待访客。

sentences.en: I'm ready.
sentences.zh: 我准备好了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Three, two, one.
sentences.zh: 三，二，一。

sentences.en: The doors slide open and all that Florida sunshine streams into the hangar, illuminating a wall of a dozen giant yellow fans stacked in two rows of six.
sentences.zh: 大门滑开，佛罗里达的阳光倾泻进机库，照亮了一面墙，上面堆叠着两排、每排六个，总共十二个巨大的黄色风扇。

sentences.en: Yeah, so there you go.
sentences.zh: 好，就是这样。

sentences.en: What do you think?
sentences.zh: 你觉得怎么样？

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Literally.
sentences.zh: 真的。

sentences.en: That's what everyone says.
sentences.zh: 每个人都这么说。

sentences.en: Never fails.
sentences.zh: 屡试不爽。

sentences.en: Each fan is six feet in diameter.
sentences.zh: 每个风扇的直径都有六英尺。

sentences.en: They were originally made for ventilating mining shafts.
sentences.zh: 它们最初是为矿井通风制造的。

sentences.en: But engineers here have figured out how to get them to make hurricane-strength winds.
sentences.zh: 但这里的工程师们想出了如何让它们产生飓风强度的风。

sentences.en: And that's why I'm here.
sentences.zh: 这就是我来这里的原因。

sentences.en: Because this is a lab where researchers are figuring out how we can make our homes and infrastructure survive hurricanes better,
sentences.zh: 因为这是一个实验室，研究人员正在研究如何让我们的房屋和基础设施更好地抵御飓风，

sentences.en: especially at a time when more intense storms are going to be more frequent.
sentences.zh: 尤其是在更强烈的风暴将变得更加频繁的时代。

sentences.en: What shape should a roof be so it stands a better chance of not getting blown off?
sentences.zh: 屋顶应该是什么形状，才能有更大的机会不被吹走？

sentences.en: Is it possible to make stronger doors?
sentences.zh: 有可能制造出更坚固的门吗？

sentences.en: What's the best kind of screw to use?
sentences.zh: 最好的螺丝是什么样的？

sentences.en: When they used to make rooftops, they would use a nail, nice and smooth.
sentences.zh: 过去他们在建造屋顶时，会使用一种光滑的钉子。

sentences.en: So when a wind comes, it's pulled right out.
sentences.zh: 所以当风吹来时，它会被直接拔出来。

sentences.en: Well, what we developed here was a nail that looks like a screw.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们在这里开发的是一种看起来像螺丝的钉子。

sentences.en: Now, if you put it into that wood, it's not going to get pulled out.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你把它钉进木头里，它就不会被拔出来。

sentences.en: You're yanking your finger and it's not moving.
sentences.zh: 你用手指去拽，它纹丝不动。

sentences.en: It's not moving.
sentences.zh: 它不动。

sentences.en: Everyone I met for this story bragged about how South Florida, which braces for hurricanes every summer,
sentences.zh: 我在做这篇报道时遇到的每个人都吹嘘南佛罗里达州是如何应对每年夏天飓风的，

sentences.en: has adopted some of the toughest building codes in the country.
sentences.zh: 他们采用了全国最严格的建筑规范。

sentences.en: And they're updated regularly, so new building methods get factored in.
sentences.zh: 而且这些规范会定期更新，以便将新的建筑方法纳入其中。

sentences.en: It's now required that all roofs use these special nails, based on research done here at the Wall of Wind.
sentences.zh: 现在要求所有屋顶都必须使用这些特殊的钉子，这是基于在“风之墙”这里所做的研究。

sentences.en: When all 12 fans are going full blast, this lab can test different construction methods
sentences.zh: 当所有12个风扇全速运转时，这个实验室可以测试不同的建筑方法，

sentences.en: against winds as high as 157 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 以抵御高达每小时157英里的风速。

sentences.en: Hurricanes that strong are incredibly rare.
sentences.zh: 那么强烈的飓风极其罕见。

sentences.en: They've only made landfall in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 它们在美国登陆的次数，

sentences.en: four times.
sentences.zh: 只有四次。

sentences.en: One of them happened right here.
sentences.zh: 其中一次就发生在这里。

sentences.en: Everyone here in South Florida, if you were down here, it's a memory that you'll never forget.
sentences.zh: 南佛罗里达的每个人，如果你当时在这里，那将是你永远不会忘记的记忆。

sentences.en: Hurricane Andrew made landfall in 1992, just south of downtown Miami.
sentences.zh: 安德鲁飓风于1992年在迈阿密市中心以南登陆。

sentences.en: Andrew had sustained winds of 165 miles per hour, destroying at least 50,000 homes,
sentences.zh: 安德鲁飓风的持续风速达到每小时165英里，摧毁了至少5万所房屋，

sentences.en: some of them, right off of their foundations.
sentences.zh: 其中一些直接从地基上被掀翻了。

sentences.en: It was the costliest disaster in U.S.
sentences.zh: 那是当时美国历史上损失最惨重的灾难。

sentences.en: history at the time.
sentences.zh: 改变了一切。

sentences.en: Changed everything.
sentences.zh: 改变了应急管理。

sentences.en: Changed emergency management.
sentences.zh: 改变了研究。

sentences.en: Changed research.
sentences.zh: 改变了建筑规范。

sentences.en: Changed the building codes.
sentences.zh: 所有这些事情在安德鲁飓风之后都得到了加速。

sentences.en: All of those things were accelerated after Hurricane Andrew.
sentences.zh: 气象学家将安德鲁飓风定为所谓的5级风暴。

sentences.en: Meteorologists designated Hurricane Andrew a so-called Category 5 storm.
sentences.zh: 即使你对飓风了解不多，你也知道5级是重大的。

sentences.en: Even if you don't know much about hurricanes, you know a Category 5 is major.
sentences.zh: 事实上，根据我们用来衡量这些事物的标准，这是最高等级。

sentences.en: It's actually the highest classification according to the scale we use to measure these things.
sentences.zh: 萨菲尔-辛普森飓风风力等级。

sentences.en: The Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale.
sentences.zh: 50年来，萨菲尔-辛普森等级一直被用来讨论如何建立更具韧性的社区。

sentences.en: For 50 years, the Saffir-Simpson scale has been used to talk about how to build more resilient communities.
sentences.zh: 它是我们所有人用来理解飓风构成何种风险的通用语言。

sentences.en: It's been the language that we all rely on to understand what kind of risk a hurricane poses.
sentences.zh: 在风暴紧急情况下，我们已经习惯于听到等级划分。

sentences.en: During storm emergencies, we are primed to hear about categories.
sentences.zh: 而且这个等级已经超越了飓风本身。

sentences.en: And the scale has transcended hurricanes.
sentences.zh: 它已被用作描述各种损害的通用简写。

sentences.en: It's been adopted as a common shorthand for describing damage of all kinds.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至在与天气完全无关的情况下使用它。

sentences.en: We use it for situations that have absolutely nothing to do with weather.
sentences.zh: 期中选举的疯狂。

sentences.en: Mid-term madness.
sentences.zh: 更像是4级飓风。

sentences.en: More like a Category 4 hurricane.
sentences.zh: 我们现在正把它当作一场巨大的5级飓风灾难来处理。

sentences.en: We're now treating this like a massive Cat 5 hurricane disaster.
sentences.zh: 国土安全部长尼尔森在那里，在移民危机面前敲响了警钟。

sentences.en: Homeland Security Secretary Nielsen there, sounding the alarm on the immigration crisis ahead of us.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普对美国政治话语来说是一场5级灾难。

sentences.en: Donald Trump is a Cat 5 disaster for American political discourse.
sentences.zh: 萨菲尔-辛普森等级之所以被如此广泛地采用，是因为它在功能上非常出色。

sentences.en: The reason the Saffir-Simpson scale has been adapted so much is because it's really good at what it does.
sentences.zh: 它是一种清晰、简单的损害简写。

sentences.en: It's a clear, easy shorthand for damage.
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们，对于不同等级的飓风强度风力，我们可以预期什么。

sentences.en: It tells us what we can expect from different categories of hurricane-strength winds.
sentences.zh: 它们可能会对我们的房屋、基础设施和社区造成什么影响。

sentences.en: What they're likely to do to our homes, to our infrastructure, and our communities.
sentences.zh: 这是可能影响的快照。

sentences.en: It's a snapshot of probable impact.
sentences.zh: 问题是，五十年过去了，我们有了不同的房屋、不同的基础设施、不同的社区。

sentences.en: The thing is, five decades on, we've got different homes, different infrastructure, different communities.
sentences.zh: 科学家们说，如今连我们的飓风都不同了。

sentences.en: Scientists say even our hurricanes are different these days.
sentences.zh: 现在人们怀疑萨菲尔-辛普森等级在那个快照中是否提供了足够的信息。

sentences.en: And there are doubts now about whether the Saffir-Simpson scale is telling us enough in that snapshot.
sentences.zh: 以及它是否仍然适用于我们生活的这个不断变化的世界。

sentences.en: And whether it still serves this changing world we live in.
sentences.zh: 因为飓风非常混乱，所以它们一直很难被准确描述。

sentences.en: Because hurricanes are so chaotic, they've always been a bit tricky to characterize.
sentences.zh: 即使在卫星和雷达时代也是如此。

sentences.en: Even in an age of satellites and radar.
sentences.zh: 它们反复无常。

sentences.en: They're capricious.
sentences.zh: 它们可以迅速增强或减弱，并改变方向。

sentences.en: They can get stronger or weaker and change direction quickly.
sentences.zh: 没有两个飓风是完全相同的。

sentences.en: No two are the same.
sentences.zh: 即使是同一个飓风，其四周也不是均匀的。

sentences.en: And even a single hurricane isn't uniform all the way around.
sentences.zh: 它们有一侧较强，另一侧较弱。

sentences.en: They have a stronger side and a weaker one.
sentences.zh: 你知道，飓风是大自然的客观事实。

sentences.en: You know, hurricanes are facts of nature.
sentences.zh: 我们能做的最好的事情就是预测它们、监测它们、了解它们，并在它们逼近时做出反应。

sentences.en: The best that we can do is forecast them, monitor them, understand them, and react to them when they do approach.
sentences.zh: 然后在它们离开后处理后果。

sentences.en: And then deal with the aftermath once they've left.
sentences.zh: 埃里克·J·多兰是《愤怒的天空》一书的作者，该书记录了美国飓风500年的历史。

sentences.en: Eric J.
sentences.zh: 在那段历史的大部分时间里……

sentences.en: Dolan is the author of A Furious Sky, the 500-year history of America's hurricanes.
sentences.zh: 飓风几乎是神秘的事件。

sentences.en: For a lot of that history...
sentences.zh: 是上帝之手的显现。

sentences.en: Hurricanes were almost mystical events.
sentences.zh: 现代预报直到19世纪中叶才出现。

sentences.en: The hand of God made manifeSt.
sentences.zh: 在此之前，作为加勒比地区原住民之一的泰诺人，教会了殖民者如何判断飓风的到来。

sentences.en: Modern forecasting didn't exist until the mid-19th century.
sentences.zh: 在了解飓风基本运作原理方面有一些小的进展。

sentences.en: Before that, the Taino, who were among the original inhabitants of the Caribbean, taught colonizers how to tell one was coming.
sentences.zh: 但直到1870年代，观察者才开始准确预测飓风从哪里来、要去哪里，以及到达时可能造成的破坏程度。

sentences.en: There were small advances in understanding the basics of how they worked.
sentences.zh: 那个巨大的飞跃来自于一位在古巴哈瓦那沿海天文台工作的耶稣会士。

sentences.en: But it wasn't until the 1870s that observers began to accurately predict where that hurricane was coming from and going to, and how destructive it might be when it got there.
sentences.zh: 他的名字叫贝尼托·维涅斯神父，但他也被称为“飓风神父”。

sentences.en: That big leap forward came from a Jesuit working out of a coastal observatory in Havana, Cuba.
sentences.zh: 该天文台拥有几十年的观测记录。

sentences.en: His name was Father Benito Vines, but he was also known as the Hurricane PrieSt.
sentences.zh: 所以他阅读、收集并系统化了这些记录。

sentences.en: The observatory had decades' worth of observations.
sentences.zh: 他拥有充足的设备，甚至还有一些是他自己发明的。

sentences.en: So he read through them, collected them, systematized them.
sentences.zh: 他每天进行多达10次测量，包括不同种类的测量，如气压测量、降水、温度等。

sentences.en: And he had plenty of equipment, even some he invented himself.
sentences.zh: 他非常热衷于观察云层。

sentences.en: He would take up to 10 measurements a day, different kinds of measurements, barometric measurements, precipitation, temperature.
sentences.zh: 那些是纤细的卷层云。

sentences.en: And he was really into watching clouds.
sentences.zh: 他称它们为猫尾云、公鸡羽毛云、风羽云。

sentences.en: Those were the wispy cirrostratus clouds.
sentences.zh: 这些云之后是更密集的云，如积层云，然后是积雨云。

sentences.en: He called them cat's tails, cock's plumes, wind feathers.
sentences.zh: 这些都是他可以用来预测恶劣天气从哪里来、要去哪里的线索。

sentences.en: And these clouds were followed by more denser clouds, cumulostratus, and then cumulonimbus.
sentences.zh: 因此，他能够对飓风及其行为方式形成非常深入的了解。

sentences.en: These were all clues that he could use to predict where bad weather was coming from and headed to.
sentences.zh: 他整理了一份相当令人印象深刻的预测记录。

sentences.en: So he was able to develop a very intimate understanding of hurricanes and how they behaved.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是运气。

sentences.en: And he put together a fairly impressive record of predictions.
sentences.zh: 维涅斯神父建立了一个电报网络，用于获取整个加勒比地区的飓风消息。

sentences.en: It was more than just chance.
sentences.zh: 他为整个地区做出的预报被刊登在报纸上，并被人们热切地阅读。

sentences.en: Father Vines set up a telegraph network for hurricane news from across the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 有人能如此精确地预测这些风暴的路径，这让人们感到震惊。

sentences.en: He made forecasts for the entire region that were printed in newspapers and eagerly read.
sentences.zh: 这位飓风神父并不总是对的。

sentences.en: It blew people's minds that someone could forecast the path of these storms with such precision.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，他和他的古巴同事凭借他们的飓风预警在国际上建立了声誉。

sentences.en: The hurricane priest didn't always get it right.
sentences.zh: 即使在维涅斯神父于1893年去世后，古巴的预报与来自其他国家的预报相比也更准确。

sentences.en: Still, he and his Cuban colleagues developed an international reputation with their hurricane warnings.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，美国的系统迟缓而保守。

sentences.en: Even after Father Vines died in 1893, Cuba's forecasts were more accurate compared to the ones from other countries.
sentences.zh: 全国各地的气象学家必须将他们的报告电报给华盛顿特区，

sentences.en: In contrast, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 由中央办公室决定什么是真实的、值得分享的。

sentences.en: system was sluggish and conservative.
sentences.zh: 预警发布缓慢，甚至根本没有发布。

sentences.en: Meteorologists around the country had to wire their reports to Washington, D.C.,
sentences.zh: 因此，当大风暴来临时，公众经常措手不及。

sentences.en: where the central office would decide what was real and worth sharing.
sentences.zh: 而且气象局的加勒比气象站是由一个认为追踪飓风是“占卜”的人管理的。

sentences.en: Warnings went out slowly, if at all.
sentences.zh: 然后情况变得更糟了。

sentences.en: So the public was frequently caught off guard when big storms arrived.
sentences.zh: 1898年，美西战争结束时，美国暂时控制了古巴，

sentences.en: And the Weather Bureau's Caribbean weather station was run by a guy who thought tracking hurricanes was, quote,
sentences.zh: 这意味着美国人控制了古巴的预警系统。

sentences.en: a matter of divination.
sentences.zh: 他们没有与加勒比地区的同事合作，

sentences.en: And then things got worse.
sentences.zh: 气象局反而限制了对电报电缆的使用，并推广他们自己的西印度群岛飓风预警系统。

sentences.en: In 1898, at the end of the Spanish-American War, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 正如我在书中描述的那样，这很大程度上与那种居高临下的态度有关。

sentences.en: took temporary control of Cuba,
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上与那种居高临下的态度有关。

sentences.en: which meant the Americans took control of Cuba's warning systeMs.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上与那种居高临下的态度有关。

sentences.en: And instead of cooperating with their colleagues in the Caribbean,
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上与那种居高临下的态度有关。

sentences.en: the Weather Bureau restricted access to telegraph cables and promoted their own West Indian hurricane warning systems instead.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上与那种居高临下的态度有关。

sentences.en: And a lot of that, as I described in the book, really had to do with the condescending attitude
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上与那种居高临下的态度有关。

sentences.en: that the American meteorologists had towards their fellow meteorologists.
sentences.zh: 美国气象学家对同行们所持有的态度。

sentences.en: And that was much to the detriment of the Americans.
sentences.zh: 而这在很大程度上损害了美国人的利益。

sentences.en: They paid the price almost immediately.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎立刻就付出了代价。

sentences.en: In September of 1900, Cuban meteorologists warned of a storm that was going to intensify,
sentences.zh: 1900年9月，古巴气象学家发出警告，称一场风暴即将增强，

sentences.en: turn into a hurricane, and head to the Gulf of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 演变成飓风，并向墨西哥湾移动。

sentences.en: And the Americans were not paying attention to the valuable meteorological information that the Cubans were providing.
sentences.zh: 而美国人并没有重视古巴人提供的宝贵气象信息。

sentences.en: And they missed some of the signs and information that the Cubans had been tracking.
sentences.zh: 他们错过了一些古巴人一直在追踪的迹象和信息。

sentences.en: They knew that it was a hurricane.
sentences.zh: 他们其实知道那是飓风。

sentences.en: It wasn't until the very last moment that the American meteorologists finally said,
sentences.zh: 直到最后一刻，美国气象学家才终于说，

sentences.en: oh, this is a hurricane.
sentences.zh: 哦，这是一场飓风。

sentences.en: By then, it was almost too late.
sentences.zh: 到那时，已经几乎太晚了。

sentences.en: Galveston's population was 38,000 people at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时加尔维斯顿的人口为3.8万人。

sentences.en: And as many as 8,000 people died.
sentences.zh: 而死亡人数多达8000人。

sentences.en: It's one thing to know, generally, that a storm is coming.
sentences.zh: 知道风暴即将来临是一回事。

sentences.en: It's another to forecast that it's going to be a deadly calamity.
sentences.zh: 预报它将成为一场致命的灾难则是另一回事。

sentences.en: And it would be decades before the U.S.
sentences.zh: 此后又过了几十年，美国才

sentences.en: began making real progress in understanding hurricanes.
sentences.zh: 在了解飓风方面取得了真正的进展。

sentences.en: That big leap came from a pair of cocky World War II pilots.
sentences.zh: 这一重大飞跃来自两名傲慢的二战飞行员。

sentences.en: The two airmen, also in Galveston, as it happens, made a bet to show how tough their planes were.
sentences.zh: 碰巧的是，这两名飞行员当时也在加尔维斯顿，他们打赌要展示自己的飞机有多结实。

sentences.en: And this was taking a plane, deliberately flying it into a hurricane, through the wall of a hurricane, into the eye of the hurricane.
sentences.zh: 这就是驾驶飞机，故意飞进飓风中，穿过飓风壁，进入飓风眼。

sentences.en: If the plane could make it, they'd get a highball.
sentences.zh: 如果飞机能成功，他们就能喝上一杯高球鸡尾酒。

sentences.en: They described the flight as being tossed around like a stick in a dog's mouth.
sentences.zh: 他们形容飞行过程就像被狗嘴里的木棍一样甩来甩去。

sentences.en: But they did make it.
sentences.zh: 但他们确实成功了。

sentences.en: And when they landed, a meteorologist from the base asked to go up next.
sentences.zh: 当他们着陆时，基地的一位气象学家请求下次也上去看看。

sentences.en: And it caught on.
sentences.zh: 于是这事儿流行开了。

sentences.en: The stunt turned into science.
sentences.zh: 这种特技演变成了科学。

sentences.en: The hurricane priest, Father Vignes, would have probably loved this.
sentences.zh: “飓风牧师”维涅斯神父可能也会喜欢这个。

sentences.en: By the early 1950s, these pilots and scientists form a cadre called hurricane hunters.
sentences.zh: 到了20世纪50年代初，这些飞行员和科学家组成了一个名为“飓风猎人”的团队。

sentences.en: They would fly directly into swirling storms, which gave them an unprecedented ability to observe hurricanes close up.
sentences.zh: 他们会直接飞进旋转的风暴中，这使他们能够前所未有地近距离观察飓风。

sentences.en: And instruments on board the planes would take measurements that could be relayed back to a land-based meteorologist or weather station with all of this data that can then be used by the meteorologist to help predict the path and strength of the hurricane.
sentences.zh: 飞机上的仪器会进行测量，并将数据传回给地面气象学家或气象站，气象学家随后利用这些数据来帮助预测飓风的路径和强度。

sentences.en: But we still didn't have a way to communicate that forecast clearly and concisely, or a way to show the public what warnings were actually based on,
sentences.zh: 但我们仍然没有一种方法来清晰简洁地传达预报，也没有一种方法向公众展示警告的依据，

sentences.en: to prove that they were worth heeding.
sentences.zh: 以证明这些警告值得重视。

sentences.en: That step was taken by the most trusted voice in broadcasting at the time, Edward R.
sentences.zh: 这一步是由当时广播界最受信任的声音爱德华·R·

sentences.en: Murrow.
sentences.zh: 默罗迈出的。

sentences.en: In mid-September of 1954, he decided to hop into a hurricane hunter plane and go and fly into the center of what was called Hurricane Edna, which was threatening the East CoaSt.
sentences.zh: 1954年9月中旬，他决定跳上一架飓风猎人飞机，飞入被称为“埃德娜”飓风的中心，当时它正威胁着东海岸。

sentences.en: Good evening.
sentences.zh: 晚上好。

sentences.en: This tattered hunk of cloth is a hurricane flag.
sentences.zh: 这块破布是一面飓风旗。

sentences.en: 1954 was an active year for hurricanes, and Edna was big news.
sentences.zh: 1954年是飓风活跃的一年，“埃德娜”是个大新闻。

sentences.en: Murrow showed the country what it was like to track a hurricane's path toward landfall.
sentences.zh: 默罗向全国展示了追踪飓风登陆路径的过程。

sentences.en: This wasn't a stunt, Murrow told viewers.
sentences.zh: 默罗告诉观众，这不是特技表演。

sentences.en: It was a routine mission, a service from the United States Air Force to the United States taxpayer.
sentences.zh: 这是一次例行任务，是美国空军为美国纳税人提供的一项服务。

sentences.en: Murrow, his cameraman, and a small flight crew climbed into a B-29 fighter plane, along with one meteorologiSt.
sentences.zh: 默罗、他的摄影师和一小队机组人员爬进了一架B-29战斗机，随行的还有一位气象学家。

sentences.en: And there was Murrow, trying to improve the public's understanding.
sentences.zh: 默罗就在那里，试图提高公众的认知。

sentences.en: The general opinion up here seems to be that Edna is not going to behave like a lady, but we will find out about that.
sentences.zh: 这里普遍的看法似乎是，“埃德娜”不会表现得像位淑女，但我们拭目以待。

sentences.en: The general opinion up here, and that's in the hurricane hunter plane, seems to be that Edna is not going to behave like a lady.
sentences.zh: 这里——也就是在飓风猎人飞机上——普遍的看法是，“埃德娜”不会表现得像位淑女。

sentences.en: So it's very 1950-ish.
sentences.zh: 所以这非常有1950年代的感觉。

sentences.en: And then the plane goes into the eyewall.
sentences.zh: 然后飞机进入了眼墙。

sentences.en: Murrow was showing the whole country, including parts far from the coasts, what the immense power of the storms looked like close up.
sentences.zh: 默罗向全国，包括远离海岸的地区，展示了风暴近距离的巨大威力。

sentences.en: What he describes into his microphone, above the roar of the engines and the storm, without even reading from a script, is beautiful.
sentences.zh: 他在引擎和风暴的轰鸣声中，甚至没有照着稿子念，对着麦克风描述的景象非常美。

sentences.en: Being in the eye was like being in an amphitheater surrounded by clouds.
sentences.zh: 身处风眼就像身处一个被云层包围的圆形剧场。

sentences.en: No sign of the sun except this dim illumination.
sentences.zh: 除了这微弱的亮光，看不到太阳的踪迹。

sentences.en: The whole surface of the ocean is undulating like some huge giant was shaking a carpet.
sentences.zh: 整个海面起伏不定，就像有个巨人正在抖动地毯。

sentences.en: Each huge wave seems to be dragging another along behind it.
sentences.zh: 每一道巨浪似乎都在身后拖着另一道浪。

sentences.en: Wrapping up, in his studio, Murrow looked into the camera for his grand summation.
sentences.zh: 在演播室里，默罗对着镜头进行了总结陈词。

sentences.en: And what he said is, in the eye of a hurricane...
sentences.zh: 他说的是，在飓风眼中……

sentences.en: In the eye of a hurricane, you learn things other than of a scientific nature.
sentences.zh: 在飓风眼中，你学到的不仅仅是科学知识。

sentences.en: You feel the puniness of man and his works.
sentences.zh: 你感受到了人类及其作品的渺小。

sentences.en: If a true definition of humility is ever written, it might well be written in the eye of a hurricane.
sentences.zh: 如果真的要给谦卑下一个定义，那它很可能就写在飓风眼中。

sentences.en: Murrow's reporting helped the public feel the pure awe of being inside a giant hurricane.
sentences.zh: 默罗的报道帮助公众感受到了身处巨大飓风内部的那种纯粹的敬畏感。

sentences.en: They could also see the enormous effort that went into tracking such a massive and dangerous phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 他们还能看到追踪这种巨大而危险的现象所付出的巨大努力。

sentences.en: A few months later, Congress set aside funds to establish the National Hurricane Research Project.
sentences.zh: 几个月后，国会拨出专款成立了国家飓风研究项目。

sentences.en: And its first director was a meteorologist named Robert Simpson.
sentences.zh: 其首任主任是一位名叫罗伯特·辛普森的气象学家。

sentences.en: That same meteorologist who was on that epic flight with Murrow.
sentences.zh: 就是那位和默罗一起进行那次史诗般飞行的气象学家。

sentences.en: Over the next few decades, Simpson became the big name in hurricane research.
sentences.zh: 在接下来的几十年里，辛普森成为了飓风研究领域的重量级人物。

sentences.en: In the early 1960s, he and his wife even led Project Storm Fury,
sentences.zh: 20世纪60年代初，他和妻子甚至领导了“风暴之怒”项目，

sentences.en: where the U.S.
sentences.zh: 美国

sentences.en: government tried to weaken hurricanes by releasing silver iodide into them.
sentences.zh: 政府试图通过向飓风中投放碘化银来削弱飓风。

sentences.en: That didn't work, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，那没成功。

sentences.en: Simpson and his colleagues were also trying to get a tighter grasp on hurricanes,
sentences.zh: 辛普森和他的同事们也试图更准确地掌握飓风的情况，

sentences.en: with enough time to warn the public about them.
sentences.zh: 以便有足够的时间向公众发出警告。

sentences.en: That meant communicating the forecast updates quickly and loudly.
sentences.zh: 这意味着要快速且大声地传达预报更新。

sentences.en: Back then, warnings for hurricanes described them in vague terms, like either minor or major.
sentences.zh: 当时，飓风的警告用语很模糊，比如“轻微”或“重大”。

sentences.en: There was a system of using flags along coastlines to tell people one was coming,
sentences.zh: 那时有一种在海岸线上使用旗帜来告诉人们风暴即将来临的系统，

sentences.en: but that was about it.
sentences.zh: 但也就仅此而已了。

sentences.en: Here's Simpson, as director of the National Hurricane Center,
sentences.zh: 这是辛普森，作为国家飓风中心主任，

sentences.en: describing his quest for a much more effective public alert system.
sentences.zh: 在描述他寻求建立一套更有效的公共预警系统的过程。

sentences.en: You can't order a model off the shelf and put it into practice.
sentences.zh: 你不能直接从货架上买个模型就投入使用。

sentences.en: But we can, through our modern technology, keep closer in touch with a hurricane,
sentences.zh: 但我们可以通过现代技术，与飓风保持更密切的联系，

sentences.en: be sure that we're not deceived.
sentences.zh: 确保我们不会被误导。

sentences.en: In 1969, a hurricane named Camille was stalled in the Gulf of Mexico.
sentences.zh: 1969年，一场名为“卡米尔”的飓风在墨西哥湾停滞不前。

sentences.en: A lady called Camille, supposedly headed toward the Florida panhandle,
sentences.zh: 一位名叫“卡米尔”的女士，本应向佛罗里达狭长地带移动，

sentences.en: but, like any lady, perfectly capable of changing her mind.
sentences.zh: 但像任何女士一样，她完全有能力改变主意。

sentences.en: Simpson didn't have a lot of information from the hurricane hunters until really late,
sentences.zh: 辛普森直到很晚才从飓风猎人那里得到大量信息，

sentences.en: because they were off chasing another storm in the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 因为他们当时正在加勒比海追逐另一场风暴。

sentences.en: He also didn't have a way to tell people, in simple terms,
sentences.zh: 他也没有办法用简单的语言告诉人们，

sentences.en: that this wasn't just going to be a hurricane.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一场普通的飓风。

sentences.en: It was going to be a hurricane.
sentences.zh: 这将会是一场大飓风。

sentences.en: The National Hurricane Center put out alerts about Camille,
sentences.zh: 国家飓风中心发布了关于“卡米尔”的警报，

sentences.en: which went beyond the simplistic language of existing warning systeMs.
sentences.zh: 其用语超出了现有预警系统的简单化语言。

sentences.en: But those meteorologists ended up giving the public too much information.
sentences.zh: 但这些气象学家最终给公众提供了太多的信息。

sentences.en: They described the storm as extremely dangerous,
sentences.zh: 他们将风暴描述为“极其危险”，

sentences.en: but also a tight little hurricane, which doesn't sound so scary, actually.
sentences.zh: 但也描述为“紧凑的小飓风”，这听起来其实没那么可怕。

sentences.en: And then they threw a lot of data at the public.
sentences.zh: 然后他们向公众抛出了大量数据。

sentences.en: They told people it had sustained winds of 150 or 160 miles per hour,
sentences.zh: 他们告诉人们，持续风速为每小时150到160英里，

sentences.en: and it was moving 12 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 移动速度为每小时12英里。

sentences.en: They reported that it had a barometric pressure of 26.81,
sentences.zh: 他们报告说气压为26.81英寸汞柱，

sentences.en: and they compared that to a terrible hurricane in 1935,
sentences.zh: 并将此与1935年的一场可怕飓风进行了比较，

sentences.en: with a barometric pressure of 26.35 inches.
sentences.zh: 那场飓风的气压为26.35英寸汞柱。

sentences.en: And I've been reporting this episode for months,
sentences.zh: 我报道这个专题已经好几个月了，

sentences.en: and I would really struggle in a crisis to tell you exactly what that comparison means.
sentences.zh: 如果真的遇到危机，我很难向你准确解释这个比较意味着什么。

sentences.en: Camille's wind speeds are now thought to have been 175 miles per hour when it made landfall.
sentences.zh: 现在认为“卡米尔”登陆时的风速为每小时175英里。

sentences.en: We don't know exactly, because the winds were so strong
sentences.zh: 我们无法确切知道，因为风力太强了，

sentences.en: that they destroyed the equipment used to record them.
sentences.zh: 以至于摧毁了记录风速的设备。

sentences.en: This scene here on the Mississippi Gulf Coast is almost like an endless nightmare.
sentences.zh: 密西西比墨西哥湾沿岸的这一幕简直就像一场无尽的噩梦。

sentences.en: Almost like an endless one-act play with some sort of a macabre ending.
sentences.zh: 几乎就像一场有着某种恐怖结局的无尽独幕剧。

sentences.en: Today, we would call Camille a Category 5 hurricane.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们会称“卡米尔”为5级飓风。

sentences.en: It's one of only four Category 5s to have ever made landfall in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 它是美国历史上仅有的四个登陆的5级飓风之一。

sentences.en: Camille killed 256 people.
sentences.zh: “卡米尔”造成256人死亡。

sentences.en: The storm washed away roads and made entire buildings just disappear.
sentences.zh: 风暴冲毁了道路，让整栋建筑直接消失。

sentences.en: People came back to their communities and found piles of debris where their homes used to be.
sentences.zh: 人们回到社区，发现曾经的家园只剩下一堆瓦砾。

sentences.en: And this is my first hurricane.
sentences.zh: 这是我经历的第一次飓风。

sentences.en: I didn't know enough to get out.
sentences.zh: 我当时不知道该撤离。

sentences.en: And my house was under 12 feet of water.
sentences.zh: 我的房子被淹在12英尺深的水下。

sentences.en: And I hope I never see nothing like this again.
sentences.zh: 我希望我再也不要看到这样的景象了。

sentences.en: One woman was speaking to a news crew about her house not being where she left it.
sentences.zh: 一位女士正在告诉新闻组，她的房子不在她离开时的地方了。

sentences.en: She turned around and saw it had been flung across the street.
sentences.zh: 她转过身，发现它被甩到了街对面。

sentences.en: And she completely lost it.
sentences.zh: 她彻底崩溃了。

sentences.en: But mine was right there on the corner and I don't even see it.
sentences.zh: 但我家就在拐角处，我甚至看不见它了。

sentences.en: Yonder!
sentences.zh: 在那边！

sentences.en: That grave and yonder that's mine.
sentences.zh: 那个坟墓那边，那是我的。

sentences.en: Bob Simpson talked about Camille in a Weather Channel documentary in 2012.
sentences.zh: 鲍勃·辛普森在2012年天气频道的一部纪录片中谈到了“卡米尔”。

sentences.en: We learned a lot from that.
sentences.zh: 我们从中学到了很多。

sentences.en: I learned a lot.
sentences.zh: 我学到了很多。

sentences.en: Both as to what kind of meteorology and what kind of language we should use
sentences.zh: 无论是关于应该使用什么样的气象学知识，还是应该使用什么样的语言，

sentences.en: that would convince the people it was a time for them to go and not to argue about it at all.
sentences.zh: 才能说服人们是时候撤离了，而不是在那儿争论不休。

sentences.en: Touring the wreckage in the Gulf, Simpson heard over and over again that local authorities wanted to know how destructive a hurricane was going to be.
sentences.zh: 在海湾地区巡视残骸时，辛普森反复听到当地官员想知道飓风会有多大的破坏力。

sentences.en: Not just numbers and readings, but a quick sense of what those numbers would mean on impact.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是数字和读数，而是对这些数字在冲击时意味着什么的直观感受。

sentences.en: What people wanted was a key to understanding the potential aftermath.
sentences.zh: 人们想要的是一把理解潜在后果的钥匙。

sentences.en: After the break, Bob Simpson teams up with a structural engineer to create the system for warning the public about deadly storMs.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，鲍勃·辛普森与一位结构工程师合作，创建了向公众预警致命风暴的系统。

sentences.en: In the wake of Hurricane Camille's devastation in 1969, one thing was clear to meteorologists like Bob Simpson.
sentences.zh: 在1969年飓风“卡米尔”造成破坏之后，像鲍勃·辛普森这样的气象学家清楚地意识到了一点。

sentences.en: The world needed a system for raiding storms that would help people understand the threat and how to respond.
sentences.zh: 世界需要一套风暴分级系统，帮助人们了解威胁并知道如何应对。

sentences.en: Someone else was already working on this, a structural engineer in Miami-Dade County named Herb Saffer.
sentences.zh: 当时已经有人在做这项工作了，他是迈阿密-戴德县的一位结构工程师，名叫赫伯·萨菲尔。

sentences.en: He was developing a hurricane scale as part of a project for the United Nations and was based on structural damage from wind.
sentences.zh: 他正在为一个联合国项目开发飓风等级，该等级基于风力造成的结构性破坏。

sentences.en: It rated hurricanes 1 through 5 based on wind speeds and described what you'd expect from each level of intensity.
sentences.zh: 它根据风速将飓风分为1到5级，并描述了每个强度等级下可能发生的情况。

sentences.en: Saffer sent his scale to the National Hurricane Center, where Bob Simpson made some tweaks, adding risks from flooding and storm surge, which is how much the sea level will rise.
sentences.zh: 萨菲尔将他的等级表发给了国家飓风中心，鲍勃·辛普森做了一些调整，增加了洪水和风暴潮（即海平面上升的高度）带来的风险。

sentences.en: And in 1974, the Saffer-Simpson Hurricane Damage Scale was first published in a scientific journal, and the National Hurricane Center started using it for the public.
sentences.zh: 1974年，“萨菲尔-辛普森飓风破坏等级”首次在科学期刊上发表，国家飓风中心开始将其用于公众预警。

sentences.en: It's just a couple of pages, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实只有几页纸。

sentences.en: Exactly a couple of pages.
sentences.zh: 确实只有几页纸。

sentences.en: Hugh Willoughby is the former director of NOAA's Hurricane Research Division.
sentences.zh: 休·威洛比是美国国家海洋和大气管理局飓风研究部的前主任。

sentences.en: He remembers when the scale was first published.
sentences.zh: 他记得该等级首次发布的时候。

sentences.en: What the categories serve is it says the wind is going to blow really hard and you want to do something about it.
sentences.zh: 这些等级的作用是告诉你风力会非常大，你需要采取行动。

sentences.en: The scale does a lot in those two pages.
sentences.zh: 这个等级表在那两页纸里做了很多工作。

sentences.en: It goes to each of the five categories.
sentences.zh: 它涵盖了全部五个等级。

sentences.en: It tells us that a Category 1 is probably going to damage mobile homes that aren't anchored to the ground, for example.
sentences.zh: 它告诉我们，例如，1级飓风可能会损坏没有固定在地面上的移动房屋。

sentences.en: Stuff you leave outside are going to become projectiles.
sentences.zh: 留在外面的东西会变成飞射物。

sentences.en: In a 2, you're going to get some widespread power outages.
sentences.zh: 在2级飓风中，你会遇到大范围的停电。

sentences.en: You can expect windows to get blown out and some signs are going to get blown away.
sentences.zh: 你可以预料到窗户会被吹破，一些标志牌会被吹走。

sentences.en: A Category 3 is where things start to get really serious, with devastating damage.
sentences.zh: 3级飓风是情况开始变得非常严重的时候，会造成破坏性的损害。

sentences.en: Trees will get uprooted or snapped, and power outages could last for weeks.
sentences.zh: 树木会被连根拔起或折断，停电可能会持续数周。

sentences.en: The scale tells us that Category 4 or above is going to be catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 该等级告诉我们，4级或以上将是灾难性的。

sentences.en: Roofs are going to come off.
sentences.zh: 屋顶会被掀掉。

sentences.en: Some walls might, too.
sentences.zh: 有些墙壁可能也会倒塌。

sentences.en: And Category 5 hurricanes are relatively rare.
sentences.zh: 而且五级飓风相对罕见。

sentences.en: Category 5 means, holy Toledo, we better do something.
sentences.zh: 五级意味着，天哪，我们最好采取行动了。

sentences.en: Cat 5s will bring power outages for months.
sentences.zh: 五级飓风会带来长达数月的停电。

sentences.en: The tops of industrial buildings will get swept off.
sentences.zh: 工业建筑的顶部会被扫平。

sentences.en: Whole structures are going to get blown away.
sentences.zh: 整个建筑物都会被吹走。

sentences.en: The categories don't ask you to know about barometric pressure.
sentences.zh: 这个分级系统并不要求你了解气压知识。

sentences.en: They don't ask you to think about whether these wind speeds are stronger than the wind speeds of the last hurricane your roof survived.
sentences.zh: 它也不要求你去思考这些风速是否比你屋顶曾抵御过的上一次飓风的风速更强。

sentences.en: The scale communicates exactly five numbers.
sentences.zh: 这个量表只传达了五个数字。

sentences.en: One to five.
sentences.zh: 一到五。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就这些。

sentences.en: You know, here's the problem.
sentences.zh: 你知道，问题就在这里。

sentences.en: 100 knots of wind sounds like a lot of wind.
sentences.zh: 100节的风速听起来风很大。

sentences.en: 150 knots of wind sounds like a lot of wind.
sentences.zh: 150节的风速听起来风也很大。

sentences.en: Hugh Willoughby likes to talk in knots, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，休·威洛比喜欢用“节”来谈论风速。

sentences.en: 100 knots is like 115 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 100节大约是每小时115英里。

sentences.en: 150 is like 172.
sentences.zh: 150节大约是172英里。

sentences.en: That's how meteorologists think about hurricanes, in these big numbers.
sentences.zh: 这就是气象学家思考飓风的方式，用这些巨大的数字。

sentences.en: But imagine using that to warn the public.
sentences.zh: 但试想一下用这种方式来警告公众。

sentences.en: That's way too much math in the middle of a crisis.
sentences.zh: 在危机时刻，这涉及的计算量太大了。

sentences.en: And the Saffir-Simpson scale gets us away from that.
sentences.zh: 而萨菲尔-辛普森飓风等级（Saffir-Simpson scale）让我们摆脱了这一点。

sentences.en: It's really useful for getting a single mom and her two kids to evacuate.
sentences.zh: 它对于促使一位单身母亲带着两个孩子撤离非常有用。

sentences.en: For 50 years, we've had categories one to five, to keep things simple.
sentences.zh: 50年来，我们一直使用一到五级的分级，以保持简单明了。

sentences.en: The reasoning was, it wasn't necessary to go any higher.
sentences.zh: 理由是，没有必要再往上分级了。

sentences.en: It's all about the property damage you can expect from a hurricane.
sentences.zh: 这完全取决于你对飓风可能造成的财产损失的预期。

sentences.en: There's a famous quote, famous to meteorologists, that is, from Bob Simpson, from a print interview he gave in 1991.
sentences.zh: 有一句名言，对气象学家来说很出名，来自鲍勃·辛普森1991年接受的一次印刷媒体采访。

sentences.en: He stuck to the scale only being about hurricane damage to buildings and infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 他坚持认为该量表仅用于衡量飓风对建筑物和基础设施的破坏。

sentences.en: Simpson explained that any storm with winds above 156 miles per hour or so, which is a Category 5,
sentences.zh: 辛普森解释说，任何风速超过每小时156英里左右的风暴，也就是五级飓风，

sentences.en: would be so awful, so devastating for buildings, that it's a catastrophe no matter what.
sentences.zh: 对建筑物来说都是极其可怕、极具破坏性的，无论如何都是一场灾难。

sentences.en: He said, quote,
sentences.zh: 他说，引用如下：

sentences.en: Quote, I think it's immaterial.
sentences.zh: “我认为这无关紧要。”

sentences.en: That's the reason why we didn't try to go any higher than that anyway.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们无论如何都没有尝试再往上分级的原因。

sentences.en: End quote.
sentences.zh: 引用结束。

sentences.en: Basically, once a building is totally destroyed, you can't get more destroyed.
sentences.zh: 基本上，一旦建筑物被彻底摧毁，它就不可能被摧毁得更严重了。

sentences.en: And an open-ended 5 accounts for that.
sentences.zh: 而一个开放式的五级涵盖了这一点。

sentences.en: But lately, there have been calls to change the scale anyway.
sentences.zh: 但最近，无论如何都有人呼吁改变这个量表。

sentences.en: Hurricane Dorian has sustained winds right now of 185 miles per hour, with gusts above 200.
sentences.zh: 飓风“多里安”目前的持续风速为每小时185英里，阵风超过200英里。

sentences.en: Hurricane Dorian sat on top of the Bahamas in 2019, dumping rain for 48 hours.
sentences.zh: 2019年，飓风“多里安”盘踞在巴哈马群岛上空，持续降雨48小时。

sentences.en: Although Dorian was technically designated a Category 5, everyone who saw it thought it was way bigger than a 5.
sentences.zh: 尽管“多里安”在技术上被定为五级飓风，但所有目睹它的人都认为它远不止五级。

sentences.en: And it was so intense that it introduced this terrifying question into the world, not just for meteorologists or researchers, but for everyone.
sentences.zh: 它太强烈了，以至于向世界提出了一个可怕的问题，不仅是对气象学家或研究人员，而是对每个人。

sentences.en: A question about how we talk about hurricanes and even how we think about them.
sentences.zh: 一个关于我们如何谈论飓风，甚至如何看待飓风的问题。

sentences.en: As we see more catastrophic hurricanes like Dorian, should scientists consider adding a Category 6 to the hurricane scale?
sentences.zh: 随着我们看到越来越多像“多里安”这样灾难性的飓风，科学家们是否应该考虑在飓风等级中增加六级？

sentences.en: A Category 6 to capture how bad things are getting.
sentences.zh: 一个六级来捕捉局势变得有多糟糕。

sentences.en: Scientists say climate change means stronger storms are going to be more frequent, and that they're likely to intensify a lot more quickly.
sentences.zh: 科学家们表示，气候变化意味着更强的风暴将更加频繁，而且它们很可能会更快地增强。

sentences.en: That's true in the Pacific, where hurricanes are called typhoons or super typhoons.
sentences.zh: 在太平洋地区确实如此，那里的飓风被称为台风或超级台风。

sentences.en: That's also true of hurricanes in the Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 在大西洋的飓风中也是如此。

sentences.en: Yes, we have seen a rash of huge hurricanes in the paSt.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们过去确实见过一连串巨大的飓风。

sentences.en: There were a bunch of them in the early 20th century.
sentences.zh: 20世纪初就有过很多次。

sentences.en: But in the last 50 years, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但在过去50年里，美国

sentences.en: has been hit by 10 hurricanes that were Category 4 or 5.
sentences.zh: 遭受了10次四级或五级飓风的袭击。

sentences.en: And seven of those giant storms have happened just since 2017.
sentences.zh: 而其中七次巨型风暴仅仅发生在2017年之后。

sentences.en: It's like we're seeing a catastrophic hurricane nearly every year.
sentences.zh: 感觉我们几乎每年都能看到一场灾难性的飓风。

sentences.en: Hurricane Harvey.
sentences.zh: 飓风“哈维”。

sentences.en: State of emergency.
sentences.zh: 进入紧急状态。

sentences.en: Tonight, Maria's direct hit, devastating Puerto Rico.
sentences.zh: 今晚，“玛丽亚”正面袭击，重创波多黎各。

sentences.en: Tonight, across Texas and Louisiana, Hurricane Laura's message, loud and clear.
sentences.zh: 今晚，横跨德克萨斯州和路易斯安那州，飓风“劳拉”发出的信息清晰响亮。

sentences.en: Hurricane Ian making history as it's making landfall.
sentences.zh: 飓风“伊恩”在登陆时创造了历史。

sentences.en: A super destructive, very dangerous phase in this Category 6.
sentences.zh: 在这个六级飓风中，一个极具破坏性、非常危险的阶段。

sentences.en: This worsening trend is why some meteorologists have started to suggest expanding the Saffir-Simpson scale to include a Category 6.
sentences.zh: 这种恶化的趋势正是为什么一些气象学家开始建议扩展萨菲尔-辛普森量表，以包括六级。

sentences.en: That conversation spilled out into the open recently with a journal article that considered what it would mean to add a Cat 6.
sentences.zh: 最近，一篇考虑增加六级意味着什么的期刊文章将这场讨论公开化了。

sentences.en: It got a ton of press attention.
sentences.zh: 它引起了媒体的极大关注。

sentences.en: The paper was called The Growing Inadequacy of an Open-Ended Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Wind Scale in a Warming World.
sentences.zh: 这篇论文的标题是《在一个变暖的世界中，开放式萨菲尔-辛普森飓风风力等级日益显现的局限性》。

sentences.en: The argument is that Category 5 has no top.
sentences.zh: 其论点是五级没有上限。

sentences.en: It starts at 157 miles per hour.
sentences.zh: 它从每小时157英里开始。

sentences.en: Sustained speed.
sentences.zh: 持续风速。

sentences.en: But where does it stop?
sentences.zh: 但它在哪里停止呢？

sentences.en: This is Richard Olson, director of the Extreme Events Institute and the International Hurricane Research Center.
sentences.zh: 这位是理查德·奥尔森，极端事件研究所和国际飓风研究中心主任。

sentences.en: Home of the wall of wind.
sentences.zh: “风墙”实验室的所在地。

sentences.en: And he's one of the people who thinks it's really time to talk about updating the scale and maybe expanding it to include a Category 6.
sentences.zh: 他是认为现在确实是时候讨论更新量表，并可能将其扩展到包括六级的人之一。

sentences.en: You look at the science and the science says, higher number of more intense storMs.
sentences.zh: 你看看科学数据，科学表明，更强烈的风暴数量在增加。

sentences.en: Okay, well, let's think about that in terms of a scale that was developed 50 years ago.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们从50年前制定的量表角度来考虑这个问题。

sentences.en: It's time to have that debate.
sentences.zh: 是时候进行那场辩论了。

sentences.en: He remembers watching Dorian's Path in 2019, when it looked like that hurricane would hit South Florida.
sentences.zh: 他记得2019年观察“多里安”的路径时，当时看起来那场飓风会袭击南佛罗里达。

sentences.en: It was going to be like Andrew all over again, only worse.
sentences.zh: 那将重演“安德鲁”飓风的惨状，甚至更糟。

sentences.en: That brought it home.
sentences.zh: 这让他感同身受。

sentences.en: It was like a lightning bolt right between my eyes.
sentences.zh: 就像一道闪电击中我的双眼之间。

sentences.en: And I said, okay, I don't know how to describe to the media what it feels like to be looking at sustained winds of 185 miles an hour, less than 30 hours from my house.
sentences.zh: 我说，好吧，我不知道该如何向媒体描述，看着距离我家不到30小时路程、持续风速达每小时185英里的飓风是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Climate change has forced scientists to make other adjustments to their extreme weather warning systeMs.
sentences.zh: 气候变化迫使科学家对他们的极端天气预警系统做出其他调整。

sentences.en: The Australian Bureau of Meteorology added two new colors, pink and purple, to their maps to convey record-breaking heat.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚气象局在地图上增加了两种新颜色，粉色和紫色，以传达破纪录的高温。

sentences.en: So maybe a 6 would expand our vocabulary for this greater risk and drive home the urgency of climate change.
sentences.zh: 所以也许六级可以扩展我们对这种更大风险的词汇量，并强化气候变化的紧迫性。

sentences.en: And the Saffir-Simpson hurricane scale is from 1974.
sentences.zh: 而萨菲尔-辛普森飓风等级是1974年的产物。

sentences.en: Maybe it could use an update.
sentences.zh: 也许它需要更新一下。

sentences.en: It describes damage as though all structures are created equal.
sentences.zh: 它描述破坏时，仿佛所有建筑都是一样的。

sentences.en: But of course that isn't true.
sentences.zh: 但当然事实并非如此。

sentences.en: Some areas have more vulnerable infrastructure than others.
sentences.zh: 有些地区的基础设施比其他地区更脆弱。

sentences.en: You could have a Category 2 storm that gives you the long-term power outages of a Category 5.
sentences.zh: 你可能会遇到一场二级风暴，却导致了五级风暴那样的长期停电。

sentences.en: Besides, a lot has changed about how we build stuff.
sentences.zh: 此外，我们在建造东西的方式上已经发生了很大变化。

sentences.en: Maybe Bob Simpson's reasoning that it's all the same damage after 5 just isn't true anymore.
sentences.zh: 也许鲍勃·辛普森关于五级以上破坏程度都一样的推论已经不再适用了。

sentences.en: It's not the same built environment as it was 30, 40 years ago.
sentences.zh: 现在的建筑环境与30、40年前已经不同了。

sentences.en: 50 even.
sentences.zh: 甚至50年前。

sentences.en: I can't believe that that's absolutely true, yes.
sentences.zh: 我无法相信那是绝对正确的，是的。

sentences.en: Now I feel really old.
sentences.zh: 现在我觉得自己真的老了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: It just says to me that we need to have the academic, government, open kind of debate.
sentences.zh: 这只是告诉我，我们需要进行学术性的、政府层面的、公开的辩论。

sentences.en: But the National Hurricane Center, which administers the scale and is in charge of categorizing hurricanes, isn't keen on adding a 6 to Saffir-Simpson.
sentences.zh: 但负责管理该量表并负责飓风分类的国家飓风中心，并不热衷于在萨菲尔-辛普森量表中增加六级。

sentences.en: There's a fear in the scientific community that expanding it would do more harm than good.
sentences.zh: 科学界有一种担忧，认为扩展它弊大于利。

sentences.en: And that's less about screws and roofs than it is about people.
sentences.zh: 这与其说是关于螺丝和屋顶，不如说是关于人。

sentences.en: What people will do when they're told about risks.
sentences.zh: 当人们被告知风险时会做什么。

sentences.en: Many don't evacuate for a 4 or 5, sometimes because they can't, sometimes because they don't want to.
sentences.zh: 许多人不会为四级或五级飓风撤离，有时是因为他们做不到，有时是因为他们不想。

sentences.en: So if 6 becomes the highest, what would that mean for the public's response?
sentences.zh: 所以如果六级成为最高级，这对公众的反应意味着什么？

sentences.en: It's still hard to understand, you know, what are we trying to achieve with calling something Category 6?
sentences.zh: 这仍然很难理解，你知道，我们试图通过称某物为六级来达到什么目的？

sentences.en: Is it meant to get people to do something different than they should be doing with a 4 or 5?
sentences.zh: 它是为了让人们做出与四级或五级时不同的行动吗？

sentences.en: This is Robbie Berg, the warning coordination meteorologist for the National Hurricane Center.
sentences.zh: 这位是罗比·伯格，国家飓风中心的预警协调气象学家。

sentences.en: The official answer from the NHC right now is no to a 6.
sentences.zh: 国家飓风中心目前的官方回答是对六级说不。

sentences.en: And then I think the next question is, is where does it stop?
sentences.zh: 然后我想下一个问题是，它在哪里停止？

sentences.en: Would they next have to add a 7?
sentences.zh: 接下来他们是否必须增加七级？

sentences.en: Some of the social science has actually shown that when you have too many categories in a scale or too many, say, colors on a map,
sentences.zh: 一些社会科学研究实际上表明，当你的量表里有太多的类别，或者地图上有太多的颜色时，

sentences.en: it actually becomes harder and harder for people to interpret that because we can't, in our minds, it's very hard to deal with too many categories.
sentences.zh: 人们反而越来越难解读，因为我们的思维很难处理太多的类别。

sentences.en: 5 is a very good, nice round number that the human mind can absorb and understand.
sentences.zh: 五是一个非常好、非常圆满的数字，人类思维可以吸收和理解。

sentences.en: And so I would say, you know, our point of view is that 4s and 5s are still catastrophic.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，你知道，我们的观点是四级和五级仍然是灾难性的。

sentences.en: What more is there than that?
sentences.zh: 除此之外还有什么？

sentences.en: And nobody's been able to answer that.
sentences.zh: 没有人能回答这个问题。

sentences.en: There's not another word beyond catastrophic that can categorize what that damage would be.
sentences.zh: 在“灾难性”之外，没有另一个词可以归类那种破坏程度。

sentences.en: I totally understand that and totally understand why they're saying, let's not run off in this direction too quickly.
sentences.zh: 我完全理解这一点，也完全理解他们为什么说，让我们不要太快朝这个方向发展。

sentences.en: Again, this is Richard Olson, who directs the International Hurricane Research Center.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，这是国际飓风研究中心主任理查德·奥尔森。

sentences.en: But I just go back to the fact that if we're seeing storms in the 180s or higher, I don't want to be playing catch-up with nature.
sentences.zh: 但我只是回到这样一个事实：如果我们看到风速在180节或更高的风暴，我不想在自然面前疲于奔命。

sentences.en: So, Olson has been thinking about what kind of research the wall of wind can contribute to the debate.
sentences.zh: 所以，奥尔森一直在思考“风墙”实验室能为这场辩论贡献什么样的研究。

sentences.en: We need to know more, he says, about what happens to our infrastructure at the further reaches of a 5.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们需要更多地了解在五级飓风的极端范围内，我们的基础设施会发生什么。

sentences.en: So the issue for us is testing at all levels, all intensities of a storm.
sentences.zh: 所以对我们来说，问题在于测试风暴的所有级别、所有强度。

sentences.en: We have to be thinking about a facility that goes beyond the current capabilities of the wall of wind.
sentences.zh: 我们必须考虑一个超越当前“风墙”实验室能力的设施。

sentences.en: That's why they've gotten a big government grant to figure out how to build a bigger, more beefed-up lab.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么他们获得了一笔巨额政府拨款，用于研究如何建造一个更大、更强大的实验室。

sentences.en: One that will go up to 200 miles per hour and have a big water tank to simulate storm surge and waves too.
sentences.zh: 一个能达到每小时200英里，并配有一个大水箱来模拟风暴潮和海浪的实验室。

sentences.en: It'd be quite large.
sentences.zh: 它会相当大。

sentences.en: Think of the wall of wind 10 times the size, probably.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，大概是“风墙”实验室的10倍大。

sentences.en: They want to simulate the whole hurricane, not just the wind part, in order to figure out how buildings and infrastructure might be able to withstand stronger storMs.
sentences.zh: 他们想模拟整个飓风，而不仅仅是风的部分，以便找出建筑物和基础设施如何能够抵御更强的风暴。

sentences.en: And that kind of facility would actually do something that goes beyond Saffir-Simpson, which points to what may be the scale's single biggest flaw.
sentences.zh: 而这种设施实际上会做一些超越萨菲尔-辛普森量表的事情，这指出了该量表可能存在的最大缺陷。

sentences.en: It doesn't at all account for water.
sentences.zh: 它根本没有考虑水。

sentences.en: It doesn't consider how much rainfall a hurricane might cause.
sentences.zh: 它没有考虑飓风可能导致多少降雨。

sentences.en: The relationship between wind speeds and storm surge isn't so simple.
sentences.zh: 风速与风暴潮之间的关系并不那么简单。

sentences.en: There are lots of complicating factors, like the angle of approach to the coast or what the continental shelf is like there.
sentences.zh: 有很多复杂的因素，比如接近海岸的角度，或者那里的大陆架是什么样的。

sentences.en: Which is why the National Hurricane Center, which administers the scale, stripped water out of the scale in 2010.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么管理该量表的国家飓风中心在2010年将水从量表中剔除的原因。

sentences.en: And yet.
sentences.zh: 然而。

sentences.en: Most people who die in hurricanes drown.
sentences.zh: 大多数死于飓风的人是溺水身亡的。

sentences.en: You know, moving water, it probably accounts for two-thirds of the property damage in almost all of the deaths.
sentences.zh: 你知道，流动的水，它可能占了几乎所有财产损失的三分之二，以及几乎所有的死亡人数。

sentences.en: Well, 80% of the deaths.
sentences.zh: 嗯，80%的死亡人数。

sentences.en: And that's what we need to worry about.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们需要担心的。

sentences.en: One way to address that would be to introduce an additional scale to warn people about flooding risk and storm surge.
sentences.zh: 解决这个问题的一种方法是引入一个额外的量表，来警告人们洪水风险和风暴潮。

sentences.en: That would save more lives.
sentences.zh: 那会挽救更多的生命。

sentences.en: The forecasters take it personally when somebody gets killed.
sentences.zh: 当有人丧生时，预报员会感到自责。

sentences.en: They just don't like it at all.
sentences.zh: 他们一点也不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And rightly so.
sentences.zh: 理应如此。

sentences.en: And the people that get drowned don't like it either.
sentences.zh: 而那些溺水的人也不喜欢这样。

sentences.en: And in fact, this is something the National Hurricane Center, the NHC, really struggles with when it comes to the Saffir-Simpson.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这正是国家飓风中心（NHC）在处理萨菲尔-辛普森量表时真正挣扎的地方。

sentences.en: It's a simple shorthand.
sentences.zh: 它是一个简单的速记法。

sentences.en: But in some ways, it's too simple.
sentences.zh: 但在某些方面，它太简单了。

sentences.en: It helps us to communicate that obviously a storm is strong when it gets to be three, four, five.
sentences.zh: 它帮助我们传达这样一个事实：当风暴达到三、四、五级时，它显然很强。

sentences.en: But we have really started to shy away from using it for everything.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实已经开始避免在所有情况下都使用它。

sentences.en: Robbie Berg with the NHC says it was a big problem during Hurricane Florence in 2018.
sentences.zh: 国家飓风中心的罗比·伯格说，这在2018年飓风“佛罗伦萨”期间是一个大问题。

sentences.en: Florence had gotten strong.
sentences.zh: “佛罗伦萨”当时已经增强了。

sentences.en: It got to a major hurricane strength.
sentences.zh: 它达到了强飓风的强度。

sentences.en: It was reaching or heading toward North Carolina.
sentences.zh: 它当时正在接近或向北卡罗来纳州移动。

sentences.en: And it began to weaken a little bit as it was approaching the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 当它接近海岸时，强度开始有所减弱。

sentences.en: It weakened so much that it was no longer technically a hurricane.
sentences.zh: 它减弱得非常厉害，以至于从技术上讲它不再是飓风了。

sentences.en: But the hazards with the storm, the rainfall we were expecting, the storm surge we were expecting, was not going to change.
sentences.zh: 但风暴带来的危险，我们预期的降雨量和风暴潮，都不会因此改变。

sentences.en: It didn't matter that the storm was weakening.
sentences.zh: 风暴是否减弱并不重要。

sentences.en: The rainfall and the surge were still going to be very bad.
sentences.zh: 降雨和风暴潮依然会非常严重。

sentences.en: So we made a concerted effort that in our communications, we did not say the storm is weakening.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们齐心协力，在沟通中刻意不去提“风暴正在减弱”。

sentences.en: They wanted people to focus on the risks of storm surge.
sentences.zh: 他们希望人们关注风暴潮的风险。

sentences.en: And wouldn't you know, as soon as we sent out the advisory, we started getting notices on our phone.
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着，我们刚发布预警，手机上就收到了各种推送。

sentences.en: And what do you think the headlines were?
sentences.zh: 你猜头条新闻是怎么写的？

sentences.en: It's weakening.
sentences.zh: 它正在减弱。

sentences.en: It's weakening.
sentences.zh: 它正在减弱。

sentences.en: It's downgraded to category one.
sentences.zh: 它已降级为一级飓风。

sentences.en: So the messages that we were intentionally trying to avoid, they were still getting out there in the media because journalists were writing stories.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们刻意想要避免传达的信息，最终还是通过媒体传播了出去，因为记者们都在写相关的报道。

sentences.en: And that's what they were attached to is the wind speed.
sentences.zh: 他们关注的重点就是风速。

sentences.en: Yeah, we suck.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我们真烂。

sentences.en: That's not what I'm saying at all.
sentences.zh: 我完全不是这个意思。

sentences.en: It's just that.
sentences.zh: 只是……

sentences.en: No, no, I'll say it.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我来说吧。

sentences.en: There's just, there's no one way that's going to fix the problem entirely.
sentences.zh: 只是，没有哪一种单一的方法能彻底解决这个问题。

sentences.en: So really, our goal is to find ways that are going to serve the most number in the population, that the most number of people are going to understand.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们真正的目标是找到能服务于最广大民众、且能被最多人理解的方法。

sentences.en: And that's just a very tricky place to get to.
sentences.zh: 要做到这一点非常困难。

sentences.en: It won't surprise you to hear that the warming climate is going to bring more and more storMs.
sentences.zh: 听到气候变暖将带来越来越多的风暴，你一定不会感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Forecasters say 2024 will be a hyperactive hurricane season with an abnormally high number of storms heading the North Atlantic.
sentences.zh: 预报员称，2024年将是一个飓风活跃期，会有异常多的风暴向北大西洋袭来。

sentences.en: And we're going into this season with extremely imperfect tools for communicating the risk.
sentences.zh: 而且我们在进入这个季节时，沟通风险的工具还非常不完善。

sentences.en: Again, here's Hugh Willoughby.
sentences.zh: 再次请出休·威洛比。

sentences.en: You know, another thing, we have hurricane watches and hurricane warnings.
sentences.zh: 你知道，还有一件事，我们有飓风观察预警和飓风警告。

sentences.en: Both begin with W, they're about the same length.
sentences.zh: 两者都以W开头，长度也差不多。

sentences.en: You know, there ought to be more psychological distance between them.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们之间应该有更明显的心理距离。

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: I can never tell what the difference is.
sentences.zh: 我永远分不清它们有什么区别。

sentences.en: Are they not just synonyms?
sentences.zh: 它们难道不是同义词吗？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: I thought I was really stupid.
sentences.zh: 我还以为是我太笨了。

sentences.en: Well, no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不是的。

sentences.en: You want the social scientists, the anthropologists, the communicators, all these people,
sentences.zh: 你需要社会科学家、人类学家、传播专家，所有这些人，

sentences.en: you want them talking to the people who do the meteorology so that you communicate it right.
sentences.zh: 你需要让他们与气象学家沟通，这样才能正确地传达信息。

sentences.en: The Category 6 debate is what got me interested in the history of how we've assessed hurricanes, and in the Saffir-Simpson scale specifically.
sentences.zh: 关于“六级飓风”的争论让我对飓风评估的历史产生了兴趣，特别是对萨菲尔-辛普森飓风等级的兴趣。

sentences.en: There have been a lot of headlines about expanding the scale to six.
sentences.zh: 关于将等级扩展到六级的头条新闻有很多。

sentences.en: There's something visceral about that idea that gets people's attention, and I totally get it.
sentences.zh: 这个想法有一种直观的冲击力，能吸引人们的注意力，我完全理解。

sentences.en: I feel it, too.
sentences.zh: 我也有同感。

sentences.en: It's both terrifying and compelling.
sentences.zh: 它既可怕又引人注目。

sentences.en: Like, things are so bad, maybe we just need to find a new way to talk about this level of bad.
sentences.zh: 就像是，情况太糟糕了，也许我们需要找到一种新的方式来描述这种程度的灾难。

sentences.en: It feels to me like we're living in six times, not just with climate change, but with wars, with failing democracies, with a global health pandemic.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们正生活在一个“六级”时代，不仅是因为气候变化，还有战争、民主制度的衰落以及全球性流行病。

sentences.en: And on and on.
sentences.zh: 诸如此类，不胜枚举。

sentences.en: But there's way less public discussion, I've found, about the fact that the scale doesn't say anything about the deadly risk from water,
sentences.zh: 但我发现，公众对于“该等级并未提及水灾带来的致命风险”这一事实的讨论要少得多，

sentences.en: or even about the urgent need to update our building codes along the coaSt.
sentences.zh: 甚至对于更新沿海建筑规范的迫切需求也讨论得不够。

sentences.en: When you think about it, those seem like pretty major blind spots.
sentences.zh: 仔细想想，这些似乎是相当大的盲点。

sentences.en: And what everyone can agree on is that we've got to address those shortcomings.
sentences.zh: 大家一致认同的是，我们必须解决这些缺陷。

sentences.en: As storms get more intense and more frequent, we need a system that rises to the occasion.
sentences.zh: 随着风暴变得越来越强烈和频繁，我们需要一个能应对挑战的系统。

sentences.en: And not just another word for catastrophe.
sentences.zh: 而不仅仅是另一个代表灾难的词汇。
